topics.name: Spasticity and Cerebral Palsy
topics.blurb: CP classification and neurosurgical spasticity management with SDR and intrathecal baclofen.

topics.blurb: Encephalocele, arachnoid cyst, Dandy-Walker, and cortical/midline developmental anomalies.

topics.name: Neurocutaneous Syndromes
topics.blurb: NF1, NF2, tuberous sclerosis, and Sturge-Weber with their neurosurgical lesions.

topics.name: Craniofacial and Positional Disorders
topics.blurb: Positional plagiocephaly counseling and congenital muscular torticollis.

topics.name: Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery

concepts.name: Hydrocephalus pathophysiology and classification
concepts.blurb: Distinguish communicating from obstructive hydrocephalus by site of CSF flow disruption.
acgme: Hydrocephalus - Pathophysiology Classification and VP Shunt

concepts.name: Hydrocephalus etiologies by age
concepts.blurb: Map dominant hydrocephalus causes onto neonatal, infant, and childhood presentations.

concepts.name: Infant hydrocephalus clinical presentation
concepts.blurb: Recognize macrocephaly, bulging fontanelle, splayed sutures, and sunsetting eyes in infants.

concepts.name: Congenital aqueductal stenosis
concepts.blurb: Obstruction at the cerebral aqueduct causing triventricular hydrocephalus, often X-linked.

concepts.name: Post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus of prematurity
concepts.blurb: Germinal matrix IVH in preterm infants obstructing CSF and producing progressive ventriculomegaly.

concepts.name: Germinal matrix IVH grading (Papile)
concepts.blurb: Grade neonatal intraventricular hemorrhage I-IV by extent and parenchymal involvement.

concepts.name: Temporizing measures for neonatal hydrocephalus
concepts.blurb: Use ventricular reservoir or ventriculosubgaleal shunt to bridge low-weight infants to permanent diversion.

concepts.name: Timing of intervention evidence (ELVIS)
concepts.blurb: Early threshold-based intervention for ventricular dilatation improves outcomes versus late drainage.

concepts.name: VP shunt hardware and valves
concepts.blurb: Identify proximal catheter, valve mechanisms, and programmable versus fixed-pressure differential valves.
acgme: Hydrocephalus - Pathophysiology Classification and VP Shunt

concepts.name: VP shunt placement technique
concepts.blurb: Place ventricular catheter and tunnel distal tubing to peritoneum with attention to neonatal anatomy.
acgme: VP Shunt in Neonates (12 Months) - Technical Considerations

concepts.name: Shunt malfunction workup
concepts.blurb: Evaluate suspected obstruction with shunt series, imaging, and reservoir assessment in symptomatic children.
acgme: VP Shunt Failure and Complications - Mechanical Obstruction Infection Over-drainage

concepts.name: Shunt infection management
concepts.blurb: Treat shunt infection with hardware removal, externalization, antibiotics, then reimplantation after CSF clearance.
acgme: VP Shunt Failure and Complications - Mechanical Obstruction Infection Over-drainage

concepts.name: Shunt reservoir tap
concepts.blurb: Aspirate the reservoir to sample CSF, assess flow, and diagnose infection or obstruction.

concepts.name: Overdrainage and slit ventricle syndrome
concepts.blurb: Recognize chronic overdrainage causing slit ventricles, low-pressure headaches, and subdural collections.
acgme: VP Shunt Failure and Complications - Mechanical Obstruction Infection Over-drainage

concepts.name: ETV indications
concepts.blurb: Select endoscopic third ventriculostomy for obstructive hydrocephalus, especially aqueductal stenosis in older infants.
acgme: Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy (ETV) and ETVCPC

concepts.name: ETV success score
concepts.blurb: Predict ETV success from age, etiology, and prior shunt to guide procedure choice.

concepts.name: ETV with choroid plexus cauterization
concepts.blurb: Combine ETV with choroid plexus cauterization to improve infant success, notably in African cohorts.
acgme: Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy (ETV) and ETVCPC

concepts.name: Arrested versus active hydrocephalus
concepts.blurb: Distinguish compensated arrested hydrocephalus from active progression needing diversion by growth and symptoms.

concepts.name: Neurulation and dysraphism embryology
concepts.blurb: Link primary and secondary neurulation failures to open versus occult dysraphic lesions.
acgme: Brain Embryology - Neural Tube Defects Cortical Development Malformations

concepts.name: Myelomeningocele
concepts.blurb: Open neural tube defect with exposed placode causing motor, sensory, and bladder deficits.
acgme: Myelomeningocele - Prenatal Detection Postnatal Repair and Associated Anomalies

concepts.name: Myelomeningocele closure technique and timing
concepts.blurb: Close the placode in watertight layers within 48-72 hours to limit infection and CSF leak.
acgme: Myelomeningocele - Prenatal Detection Postnatal Repair and Associated Anomalies

concepts.name: Fetal MMC repair (MOMS trial)
concepts.blurb: Prenatal closure reduces shunt dependence and improves motor function versus postnatal repair.

concepts.name: Prenatal counseling for dysraphism
concepts.blurb: Counsel families on prognosis, fetal versus postnatal repair, and associated anomalies after prenatal diagnosis.

concepts.name: Chiari II malformation
concepts.blurb: Hindbrain herniation with brainstem and vermis descent, nearly universal in open myelomeningocele.
acgme: Chiari Malformation Type II III and Syringomyelia

concepts.name: Lipomyelomeningocele
concepts.blurb: Closed lipomatous mass tethering the cord; prophylactic surgery versus observation remains controversial.
acgme: Tethered Spinal Cord - Filum Terminale Section Lipomyelomeningocele

concepts.name: Dorsal dermal sinus tract
concepts.blurb: Epithelial tract from skin to neural tissue risking infection, dermoid, and tethering.

concepts.name: Split cord malformation
concepts.blurb: Diastematomyelia type I has bony septum and dual dural sacs; type II shares one sac.

concepts.name: Tethered cord syndrome
concepts.blurb: Progressive neuro-urologic and orthopedic decline from abnormal caudal cord traction.
acgme: Tethered Spinal Cord - Filum Terminale Section Lipomyelomeningocele

concepts.name: Spinal cord detethering
concepts.blurb: Section filum or release adhesions to halt progression, weighing retethering risk and monitoring.
acgme: Tethered Spinal Cord - Filum Terminale Section Lipomyelomeningocele

concepts.name: Occult dysraphism cutaneous markers
concepts.blurb: Identify hairy patch, dimple, hemangioma, or lipoma prompting spinal imaging for occult dysraphism.

concepts.name: Neurogenic bladder in dysraphism
concepts.blurb: Manage detrusor dysfunction with urodynamics and clean intermittent catheterization to protect renal function.

concepts.name: Craniosynostosis pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Premature suture fusion restricts perpendicular growth, producing predictable compensatory skull deformities.

concepts.name: Sagittal synostosis (scaphocephaly)
concepts.blurb: Most common synostosis producing a long, narrow boat-shaped skull with frontal bossing.
acgme: Craniosynostosis - Sagittal Synostectomy (Suturectomy)

concepts.name: Unicoronal synostosis (anterior plagiocephaly)
concepts.blurb: Unilateral coronal fusion causing ipsilateral forehead flattening and harlequin orbit deformity.

concepts.name: Metopic synostosis (trigonocephaly)
concepts.blurb: Metopic fusion yields a triangular forehead with keel ridge and hypotelorism.

concepts.name: Lambdoid synostosis
concepts.blurb: Rare true posterior synostosis producing trapezoid skull with posteriorly displaced ipsilateral ear.

concepts.name: Bicoronal synostosis (brachycephaly)
concepts.blurb: Bilateral coronal fusion shortens the skull anteroposteriorly, often signaling syndromic disease.

concepts.name: Positional plagiocephaly
concepts.blurb: Deformational flattening producing parallelogram head with ipsilateral anterior ear, no suture fusion.

concepts.name: Syndromic craniosynostosis and FGFR
concepts.blurb: Apert, Crouzon, and Pfeiffer arise from FGFR mutations with multisuture fusion and midface hypoplasia.

concepts.name: Elevated ICP in syndromic synostosis
concepts.blurb: Multisuture syndromic fusion raises intracranial pressure risk, threatening vision and development.

concepts.name: Endoscopic strip craniectomy with helmet
concepts.blurb: Early endoscopic suturectomy plus postoperative helmet remodels skull in infants under six months.
acgme: Craniosynostosis - Sagittal Synostectomy (Suturectomy)

concepts.name: Open cranial vault remodeling
concepts.blurb: Open calvarial reconstruction reshapes the skull, typically after six months for definitive correction.
acgme: Craniosynostosis - Fronto-Orbital Advancement and Cranial Vault Reconstruction

concepts.name: Fronto-orbital advancement
concepts.blurb: Advance the supraorbital bar and forehead to correct anterior synostoses and protect the orbits.
acgme: Craniosynostosis - Fronto-Orbital Advancement and Cranial Vault Reconstruction

concepts.name: Chiari I definition and measurement
concepts.blurb: Define Chiari I as cerebellar tonsillar descent at least five millimeters below foramen magnum.
acgme: Chiari Malformation Type I - Suboccipital Decompression (12 months)

concepts.name: Chiari I natural history
concepts.blurb: Many incidental Chiari I remain stable, so asymptomatic descent often warrants observation.

concepts.name: Chiari I clinical presentation
concepts.blurb: Suspect Chiari I with cough-induced occipital headache, and lower cranial or cerebellar signs.

concepts.name: Syringomyelia association
concepts.blurb: Chiari-associated syrinx causes cape sensory loss; decompression often drives syrinx regression.
acgme: Chiari Malformation Type II III and Syringomyelia

concepts.name: Chiari decompression indications
concepts.blurb: Operate for symptomatic Chiari, progressive syrinx, or myelopathy rather than incidental descent.

concepts.name: Posterior fossa decompression technique
concepts.blurb: Suboccipital craniectomy with C1 laminectomy, with or without duraplasty, relieves crowding.
acgme: Chiari Malformation Type I - Suboccipital Decompression (12 months)

concepts.name: Complex Chiari and basilar invagination
concepts.blurb: Complex Chiari with basilar invagination or instability may require occipitocervical fixation.

concepts.name: Posterior fossa tumor differential
concepts.blurb: Differentiate medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, ependymoma, and ATRT by location and imaging.
acgme: Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumors (Medulloblastoma Ependymoma Astrocytoma)

concepts.name: Medulloblastoma
concepts.blurb: Malignant midline cerebellar embryonal tumor with CSF dissemination risk in children.
acgme: Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumors (Medulloblastoma Ependymoma Astrocytoma)

concepts.name: Medulloblastoma molecular groups
concepts.blurb: Stratify into WNT, SHH, group 3, and group 4 with divergent prognosis and therapy.

concepts.name: Pilocytic astrocytoma
concepts.blurb: Benign WHO grade 1 cystic tumor with mural nodule and BRAF fusion; resection often curative.

concepts.name: Posterior fossa ependymoma
concepts.blurb: Fourth ventricular tumor with PFA and PFB subgroups; extent of resection drives outcome.
acgme: Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumors (Medulloblastoma Ependymoma Astrocytoma)

concepts.name: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor
concepts.blurb: Aggressive infant embryonal tumor with SMARCB1/INI1 loss and poor prognosis.

concepts.name: DIPG and diffuse midline glioma
concepts.blurb: Diffuse midline glioma with H3 K27M alteration; pontine DIPG is treated with radiation, not resection.
acgme: Brainstem Glioma or DIPG and Biopsy

concepts.name: Posterior fossa syndrome (cerebellar mutism)
concepts.blurb: Delayed mutism, emotional lability, and ataxia after midline cerebellar tumor resection.

concepts.name: Posterior fossa tumor management
concepts.blurb: Address hydrocephalus, resect via midline suboccipital approach, and stage adjuvant therapy by pathology.

concepts.name: Hydrocephalus from posterior fossa tumor
concepts.blurb: Manage obstructive hydrocephalus from fourth ventricle tumors with steroids, EVD, ETV, or resection.

concepts.name: CSF dissemination and staging
concepts.blurb: Stage embryonal tumors with neuraxis MRI and CSF cytology to detect drop metastases.

concepts.name: Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma
concepts.blurb: Calcified cystic sellar tumor with motor oil fluid causing visual and endocrine deficits.
acgme: Pediatric Craniopharyngioma - Surgical Approach and Endocrinology Management

concepts.name: Optic pathway glioma and NF1
concepts.blurb: Low-grade glioma along optic apparatus, strongly associated with NF1, often managed without resection.

concepts.name: Intracranial germ cell tumors
concepts.blurb: Pineal and suprasellar germinomas and NGGCTs stratified by AFP and beta-hCG markers.
acgme: Pediatric Pineal Region Tumors - ETV and Resection

concepts.name: Choroid plexus tumors of infancy
concepts.blurb: Intraventricular papilloma or carcinoma causing CSF overproduction and hydrocephalus in infants.
acgme: Choroid Plexus Tumors (Papilloma Carcinoma)

concepts.name: Supratentorial pediatric tumor overview
concepts.blurb: Survey supratentorial childhood tumors including gliomas, craniopharyngioma, and germ cell tumors.
acgme: Pediatric Supratentorial Tumor Resection

concepts.name: Infantile brain tumors
concepts.blurb: Large tumors of infancy such as DIG/DIA and ETMR pose resection and chemotherapy challenges.

concepts.name: Vein of Galen malformation
concepts.blurb: Choroidal arteriovenous shunt into median prosencephalic vein causing neonatal high-output heart failure.

concepts.name: Vein of Galen management
concepts.blurb: Stage staged endovascular embolization using the Bicetre score to time treatment around cardiac status.

concepts.name: Pediatric arteriovenous malformation
concepts.blurb: AVMs are the leading cause of pediatric spontaneous hemorrhage with high lifetime rupture risk.

concepts.name: Pediatric moyamoya
concepts.blurb: Progressive supraclinoid ICA stenosis with collateral puff-of-smoke causing ischemic strokes in children.
acgme: Moyamoya Disease - Diagnosis Angiographic Staging and Revascularization

concepts.name: Indirect revascularization (pial synangiosis)
concepts.blurb: Pial synangiosis or EDAS recruits external carotid collaterals to perfuse ischemic pediatric cortex.
acgme: Moyamoya Disease - Diagnosis Angiographic Staging and Revascularization

concepts.name: Perinatal stroke
concepts.blurb: Arterial ischemic or venous perinatal stroke presents with seizures or later hemiparesis.

concepts.name: Abusive head trauma recognition
concepts.blurb: Suspect inflicted injury when intracranial findings exceed the reported mechanism in young infants.
acgme: Abusive Head Trauma (Shaken Baby Syndrome) - Diagnosis and Legal Considerations

concepts.name: Subdural patterns in abusive head trauma
concepts.blurb: Multiple ages of subdural blood and interhemispheric collections suggest repetitive inflicted injury.

concepts.name: Retinal hemorrhage in AHT
concepts.blurb: Multilayered hemorrhages reaching the ora serrata strongly support abusive head trauma.

concepts.name: Abusive versus accidental injury
concepts.blurb: Weigh history consistency, injury pattern, and development to distinguish abuse from accidental trauma.

concepts.name: Birth-related scalp injuries
concepts.blurb: Differentiate caput succedaneum, cephalohematoma, and subgaleal hemorrhage by boundaries and risk.

concepts.name: Cephalohematoma
concepts.blurb: Subperiosteal blood collection bounded by sutures, usually benign and self-resolving.

concepts.name: Subgaleal hemorrhage
concepts.blurb: Blood in the subaponeurotic space crosses sutures and can cause life-threatening neonatal blood loss.

concepts.name: Growing skull fracture
concepts.blurb: Diastatic fracture with dural tear enlarges as a leptomeningeal cyst in young children.

concepts.name: Pediatric Glasgow Coma Scale
concepts.blurb: Apply the modified verbal and motor GCS scale to preverbal infants and young children.

concepts.name: SCIWORA
concepts.blurb: Spinal cord injury without radiographic abnormality reflects ligamentous laxity in young children.
aliases: spinal cord injury without radiographic abnormality

concepts.name: Cervical pseudosubluxation
concepts.blurb: Physiologic C2-C3 anterior displacement in children mimics injury; the spinolaminar line stays intact.

concepts.name: Pediatric cervical spine laxity
concepts.blurb: Large head, lax ligaments, and horizontal facets shift the fulcrum and injury pattern upward.

concepts.name: Cerebral palsy overview
concepts.blurb: Nonprogressive motor disorder from early brain injury producing spasticity, dystonia, or mixed tone.

concepts.name: Gross Motor Function Classification System
concepts.blurb: Stratify cerebral palsy mobility into five levels guiding surgical spasticity candidacy.

concepts.name: Selective dorsal rhizotomy candidacy
concepts.blurb: SDR best suits ambulatory spastic diplegia with good strength and selective dorsal rootlet sectioning.
acgme: Surgical Management of Spasticity (ITB Selective Dorsal Rhizotomy)

concepts.name: Intrathecal baclofen in children
concepts.blurb: Implanted baclofen pump treats severe generalized spasticity and dystonia across mobility levels.
acgme: Surgical Management of Spasticity (ITB Selective Dorsal Rhizotomy)

concepts.name: Encephalocele
concepts.blurb: Herniation of meninges and brain through a skull defect, classified by location.
acgme: Encephalocele - Classification and Surgical Repair

concepts.name: Arachnoid cyst management
concepts.blurb: Most arachnoid cysts are incidental; treat only symptomatic or enlarging lesions, debating fenestration versus shunt.
acgme: Arachnoid Cysts - Fenestration vs Cystoperitoneal Shunt

concepts.name: Dandy-Walker malformation
concepts.blurb: Vermian hypoplasia, cystic fourth ventricle, and enlarged posterior fossa with frequent hydrocephalus.
acgme: Dandy-Walker Malformation - Spectrum and Management

concepts.name: Agenesis of the corpus callosum
concepts.blurb: Callosal agenesis with colpocephaly and Probst bundles; significance ranges from incidental to syndromic.

concepts.name: Hydranencephaly
concepts.blurb: Near-total cortical destruction with preserved thalami and falx, distinct from maximal hydrocephalus.

concepts.name: Malformations of cortical development
concepts.blurb: Lissencephaly, heterotopia, polymicrogyria, and focal cortical dysplasia frequently underlie pediatric epilepsy.
acgme: Brain Embryology - Neural Tube Defects Cortical Development Malformations

concepts.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
concepts.blurb: NF1 features cafe-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, optic gliomas, and a tumor-suppressor mutation.

concepts.name: Neurofibromatosis type 2
concepts.blurb: NF2 causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas, meningiomas, and ependymomas from chromosome 22 loss.

concepts.name: Tuberous sclerosis complex
concepts.blurb: TSC features cortical tubers, subependymal nodules, SEGA, and seizures from TSC1/TSC2 mutation.

concepts.name: SEGA and mTOR inhibitors
concepts.blurb: Subependymal giant cell astrocytomas near the foramen of Monro respond to mTOR inhibitor everolimus.

concepts.name: Sturge-Weber syndrome
concepts.blurb: Leptomeningeal angiomatosis with facial port-wine stain, seizures, and tram-track calcifications.

concepts.name: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
concepts.blurb: VHL predisposes to CNS hemangioblastomas, retinal angiomas, and renal cell carcinoma.

concepts.name: Positional plagiocephaly counseling
concepts.blurb: Counsel repositioning, tummy time, and selective helmet therapy for deformational plagiocephaly without surgery.

concepts.name: Congenital muscular torticollis
concepts.blurb: Sternocleidomastoid fibrosis tilts the head and contributes to positional plagiocephaly; physiotherapy is first-line.

concepts.name: Pediatric epilepsy surgery candidacy
concepts.blurb: Evaluate drug-resistant pediatric epilepsy for resective or disconnective surgery via multimodal localization.

concepts.name: Hemispherotomy
concepts.blurb: Functional disconnection of a hemisphere controls catastrophic unilateral epilepsy with less resection than hemispherectomy.
acgme: Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery - Hemispherectomy Multi-Lobar Resection

concepts.name: Hemispheric surgery indications
concepts.blurb: Hemimegalencephaly, Rasmussen encephalitis, and Sturge-Weber drive unilateral hemispheric epilepsy surgery.
acgme: Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery - Hemispherectomy Multi-Lobar Resection
